# Environmental Computing 👋

**[Environmental Computing](https://environmentalcomputing.net/)** is a free online book of tutorials on R coding, data handling, graphics and statistics for environmental scientists. It began as teaching material for courses at UNSW Sydney, and is written by researchers, for researchers and students. More about the site is in the [preface](https://environmentalcomputing.net/content/preface.html).

The book covers:

- **Basics:** installing R and RStudio, and organising projects
- **Data literacy:** importing, subsetting, combining, reshaping and summarising data
- **Data visualisation:** ggplot2, multi-panel figures, rasters and maps
- **Statistical methods:** t-tests, linear models, ANOVA, GLMs, mixed models, GAMs, meta-analysis and multivariate methods
- **Coding skills:** good practice, functions, loops, version control and asking code questions

The book is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/). Pages that moved from the old Hugo and WordPress sites still work, because their old addresses redirect to the matching chapters.

## Found a problem or want a new tutorial?

[Open an issue](https://github.com/nicercode/EnvironmentalComputing/issues). Every page also has "Edit this page" and "Report an issue" links.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome, from typo fixes to whole tutorials. Read the [contributing guide](content/contributing.qmd) first. It covers file layout, naming, where images and data go, and caching.

To build the book locally, you need [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) and [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/nicercode/EnvironmentalComputing.git
cd EnvironmentalComputing
Rscript -e 'install.packages("remotes"); remotes::install_deps()'   # packages from DESCRIPTION
quarto preview                                                        # live preview in your browser
```

Things to know before opening a pull request:

- **Commit `_freeze/`.** Chapters are only re-run when their source changes. After editing a chapter, render it (`quarto render path/to/chapter.qmd`) and commit the updated `_freeze/` entry along with it.
- **Add new packages to `DESCRIPTION`**, in alphabetical order, so CI can install them.
- **Keep old addresses working.** `_redirects` sends old site addresses to book chapters and sections. If you move or rename a chapter, or change a heading that a redirect points to, update the matching lines there; CI checks every redirect still lands somewhere.
- **Every pull request gets a deploy preview.** It is linked in a comment on the PR, and CI checks that every chapter renders without errors and that internal links work.

## How the site is deployed

The site is hosted on [Netlify](https://app.netlify.com/sites/environmentalcomputing/deploys), on Daniel Falster's (@dfalster) Netlify account. Ask him for access.

Netlify does not build the site itself, because its build image cannot run the R code. Instead, GitHub Actions ([.github/workflows/book.yml](.github/workflows/book.yml)) renders the book and uploads `_book/` to Netlify:

- every push to `master` deploys to the live site, environmentalcomputing.net;
- every pull request gets a deploy preview, linked in a comment on the PR;
- once a month, a scheduled run re-renders every chapter from scratch and checks external links. If a tutorial has broken (for example, after a package update), it opens an issue;
- `netlify.toml` tells Netlify to skip its own builds (`ignore = "exit 0"`).

The upload needs two repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):

- `NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`: a personal access token from dfalster's Netlify account (User settings → Applications → Personal access tokens);
- `NETLIFY_SITE_ID`: the Site ID of the `environmentalcomputing` site (Site configuration → Site details). Do not use the other site, `friendly-albattani-0a0cb6`.

If either secret is missing, CI on `master` fails at the "Check Netlify credentials" step; if the token has expired or been revoked, it fails at "Deploy to Netlify". Either way the live site stops updating until the secret is replaced: create a new token and run `gh secret set NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN`.

Old site addresses are redirected to book chapters by `_redirects`, which is copied into `_book/` at render time. It was first generated when the site moved from Hugo to Quarto in 2026; [migration/](migration/README.md) records how that port was done.

## Contributors

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide

suppressPackageStartupMessages(
library(tidyverse)
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
contribs_all_json <- gh::gh("/repos/:owner/:repo/contributors",
  owner = "nicercode",
  repo = "EnvironmentalComputing",
  .limit = Inf
)

contribs_all <- tibble(
  login = contribs_all_json |> map_chr("login"),
  n = contribs_all_json |> map_int("contributions")
)

contribs_old <- read_csv("contributors.csv", col_types = list())
contribs_new <- contribs_all |> anti_join(contribs_old, by = "login")

# Get info for new contributors
needed_json <- map(
  contribs_new$login,
  ~ gh::gh("/users/:username", username = .x),
  .progress = TRUE
)
info_new <- tibble(
  login = contribs_new$login,
  name = map_chr(needed_json, "name", .default = NA),
  blog = map_chr(needed_json, "blog", .default = NA)
)
info_old <- contribs_old |> select(login, name, blog)
info_all <- bind_rows(info_old, info_new)

contribs_all <- contribs_all |>
  left_join(info_all, by = "login") |>
  mutate(login_lowercase = str_to_lower(login)) |>
  arrange(login_lowercase) |>
  select(-login_lowercase)
write_csv(contribs_all, "contributors.csv")
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
#| message: false
# List adapted from the R for Data Science README (https://github.com/hadley/r4ds)
contributors <- readr::read_csv("contributors.csv")
contributors <- contributors |>
  filter(!login %in% c("nicercode", "dfalster", "wcornwell", "fontikar", "alistairpoore")) |>
  mutate(
    profile = paste0("[@", login, "](https://github.com/", login, ")"),
    desc = ifelse(is.na(name), profile, paste0(name, " (", profile, ")"))
  )

cat("Thanks to everyone who has contributed new content and fixes on GitHub:\n\n")
cat(paste0("- ", contributors$desc, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```
